media_work.title: Stolen Years (20/20)
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful murder conviction, systemic resistance to acknowledging innocence despite DNA
media_work.summaryNotes: Case involved 3 convictions despite exculpatory DNA.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful murder conviction, systemic resistance to acknowledging innocence despite DNA
media_item.summary_notes: This 20/20 episode investigates how Juan Rivera was convicted three times despite DNA evidence pointing to another individual, exploring systemic resistance to acknowledging innocence. The case is a stark example of repeated convictions despite exculpatory DNA.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Investigates how Rivera was convicted three times despite DNA pointing to another; Explores systemic resistance. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: While a specific 20/20 episode titled "Stolen Years" wasn't confirmed via search, the details provided in `film_list.txt` accurately describe the well-known Juan Rivera case from Lake County, Illinois. His case is a stark example of repeated convictions despite exculpatory DNA.

featured_individuals.sentence: Life in prison (received in third trial)
featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Rape and Murder (of 11-year-old Holly Staker in 1992)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Juan Rivera was wrongfully convicted of the rape and murder of Holly Staker and served nearly 20 years in prison. He was convicted three times despite DNA evidence excluding him. His conviction was overturned on appeal and he won a civil rights lawsuit.
contributing_factors_raw: convicted three times despite DNA evidence excluding him and pointing elsewhere
alleged police/prosecutorial misconduct (planting evidence alleged in lawsuit)
